proposal.title: Select MiniScribe 4010 for Athena and Quantum Q540 for Athena Server
proposal.reason: Author confirms Athena PRO means existing Athena Server. Both existing offerings already contain one FDD and one HDD; update their canonical HDD assemblies rather than duplicate product configuration. Use the specified unformatted capacities, with usable capacity established by controller format. Reconcile host requirements, engineering assumptions and the premiere description. Quantum $1,485 is the supplied OEM benchmark (previous research: 100-unit pricing); no 1,000-unit discount is inferred. Keep the older Rodime part as an unused historical definition rather than deleting it without instruction. Q540 premiere use is a planning selection, not proof of volume availability.

chapters.description:
Logix Athena — base computer uses a desktop/server chassis built around {processor_id}.

Its EEPROM BIOS boots and initializes hardware, runs diagnostics and selects ROM-based AIONix2/recovery or disk patches. BIOS capacity and chassis mechanics remain unspecified. External application ROM cards are not supported.

Installed RAM must satisfy the selected configuration, and a monitor must connect to a fitted video provider. The internal system cartridge does not establish support for external application cartridges.

The base computer is supplied without a graphics card. Display capabilities are defined by the card and monitor selected for the complete system.

Two matched 32-bit modules form each capacity bank, selected independently on the shared bus. Fill banks in order; decode and refresh every rank. Replace the population when changing density rather than mixing module types. Cross-host connector and timing qualification remains open. Maximum motherboard RAM and socket count remain unspecified and are distinct from the CPU address-space limit.

A replaceable cartridge supplies {system_rom_bytes} bytes of shared executable AIONix2 code; private writable state and patch overlays consume DRAM. Cartridge chip organization, connector, timing and exchange procedure require qualification. {recommended_system_id} preserves documented ERA/AIONix binaries through versioned compatibility, with individual editions still requiring qualification.

before.title: NCC 1983: planned ERA² and Logix Athena premiere
before.description: Present ERA² at 12 MHz target (16 MHz stretch), Athena 256 KiB / 5 MB HDD and Athena Server 1 MiB / 20 MB HDD. Both include 64 KiB graphics, one 5.25-inch DS/DD floppy and one network card. EEPROM BIOS plus 256 KiB directly executable AIONix2 system ROM. Protected multitasking, legacy ERA ABI, recoverable HDD storage, users and layered TUI are accepted design targets, pending implementation qualification. Conference runs 16–19 May in Anaheim; premiere does not certify volume shipments.

inputs.description: An ERA² implementation suitable for the demonstrated Athena configuration is required for the premiere. The wider development programme continues through the subsequent production review; this input does not claim that programme completion or volume-shipment qualification precedes the premiere.
Present the AIONix2 design targets and implementation status for Athena, explicitly distinguishing them from qualified production availability.

after.title: NCC 1983: planned ERA² and Logix Athena premiere
after.description: Present ERA² at 12 MHz target (16 MHz stretch), Athena 256 KiB with a MiniScribe 4010 HDD (10 MB unformatted) and Athena Server 1 MiB with a Quantum Q540 HDD (approximately 43 MB unformatted). Usable capacity is lower after formatting. Both include 64 KiB graphics, one 5.25-inch DS/DD floppy and one network card. EEPROM BIOS plus 256 KiB directly executable AIONix2 system ROM. Protected multitasking, legacy ERA ABI, recoverable HDD storage, users and layered TUI are accepted design targets, pending implementation qualification. Conference runs 16–19 May in Anaheim; premiere does not certify volume shipments.

AIONix2 has an accepted phased design baseline; implementation and measured fit remain qualification gates.
All ERA² architectural numbers are engineering targets, with 16 MHz a stretch bin.
AION Labs alone manufactures ERA² initially; SGS-ATES excluded for at least 12–18 months after initial commercial availability.
Development dates are provisional; cost and financial forecasts remain unchanged.
